content: The protein known as Coiled-coil domain containing 137 (CCDC137) is encoded by the CCDC137 gene in humans. Model organisms have been utilized to investigate the function of CCDC137. Specifically, a conditional knockout mouse line, named Ccdc137<tm1a(KOMP)Wtsi>, was developed as part of the International Knockout Mouse Consortium program. This program is a high-throughput mutagenesis initiative aimed at creating and distributing animal models of human diseases to researchers. The mouse line was generated at the Wellcome Trust Sanger Institute. Both male and female mice underwent a standardized phenotypic screening process to assess the effects of the gene deletion. A total of 25 tests were conducted on the mutant mice, and two significant abnormalities were identified. No homozygous mutant embryos were detected during gestation. Furthermore, in a separate study, no homozygous animals were observed at the weaning stage. The remaining tests were performed on adult heterozygous mutant animals, but no additional abnormalities were identified.
